title: Making, moving and declining plans (Verabredungen)
summary: Ask if someone has time, say yes or no politely, move a time, and say you're late: with friends (du), colleagues (Sie) and classmates.
goals: Ask if someone has time and suggest something
Say yes, or say no politely with a reason
Make an appointment with a colleague (Sie)

sections.title: Saying no nicely
sections.text:
A German no is short but friendly. Use [[leider]] (unfortunately) or [[Tut mir leid]] (I'm sorry), give a reason with [[müssen]], and suggest something else:

[[Am Samstag kann ich leider nicht. Ich muss arbeiten. Geht es auch am Sonntag?]]

The other person may answer [[Schade!]] (too bad) or [[Kein Problem!]]

[[Tut mir leid]] literally means 'it does me sorrow'. It's a fixed phrase; Unit 6 explains [[mir]].

sections.title: Moving a time, and being late
sections.text:
- [[Um drei kann ich nicht. Geht es auch um vier?]] = I can't at three. Does four work too?
- [[Ich habe am Nachmittag frei. Geht es am Nachmittag?]] = I'm free in the afternoon. Does the afternoon work?
- [[Ich komme zehn Minuten später.]] = I'll be ten minutes late. (Literally: I come ten minutes later.)
- [[Tut mir leid, ich bin zu spät!]] = Sorry, I'm late!

[[Das geht]] = that works. [[Das geht nicht]] = that doesn't work. [[Geht es ...?]] = does ... work?

When the main verb is clear, Germans drop it: [[Um drei kann ich nicht.]] means [[Um drei kann ich nicht kommen.]] Same with [[Tut mir leid, ich kann nicht.]] and [[Vielleicht kann ich am Sonntag.]]

sections.title: Wir treffen uns
sections.text:
[[Wir treffen uns]] = we meet (each other). The [[uns]] works like Russian -ся in встречаемся. Verbs like this come properly at A2; for now it's a chunk:
- [[Wir treffen uns um sieben.]]
- [[Wann treffen wir uns?]]

sections.title: At work: appointments with Sie
sections.text:
With your boss, a colleague you don't know well, or an office, use [[Sie]] and [[der Termin]]:
- [[Haben Sie am Dienstag Zeit?]]
- [[Der Termin ist am Dienstag um zehn Uhr.]]
- [[Geht es auch um elf?]] - [[Ja, das geht.]]
- [[Ich habe um drei einen Termin.]] ([[einen]]: the Unit 2 chunk after [[haben]])

Be [[pünktlich]] (on time) for a [[Termin]]. With friends, five minutes late is normal if you send a message first.
Two phrases from lesson 3 are perfect for the end of a plan: [[Ich rufe dich an.]] = I'll call you. [[Ich hole dich ab.]] = I'll pick you up. [[Gut, ich hole dich um sieben ab. Bis dann!]]

items.de: Hallo Eva! Hast du am Samstag Zeit?
items.en: Hi Eva! Are you free on Saturday?

items.de: Wollen wir ins Kino gehen? Der Film fängt um drei an.
items.en: Shall we go to the cinema? The film starts at three.

items.de: Um drei kann ich leider nicht. Ich muss einkaufen. Geht es auch um sechs?
items.en: Unfortunately I can't at three. I have to do the shopping. Does six work too?

items.de: Ja, das geht. Der Film fängt um sechs an. Wir treffen uns um Viertel vor sechs.
items.en: Yes, that works. The film starts at six. Let's meet at quarter to six.
Unfortunately not. I have to work.

items.de: Tut mir leid, ich bin zu spät!

items.question: Your friend asks: 'Hast du am Freitag Zeit?' You're busy. What do you say?
items.explanation: A friendly no: leider, then a reason with müssen.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: Three o'clock? Yes, that works.
items.explanation: Das geht = that works. Das geht nicht = that doesn't work.
Wir treffen uns is a chunk. With the time first: Um sieben treffen wir uns.
kann in second place, kommen at the end. leider can start the sentence (then the verb follows) or come after the verb.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I'll be ten minutes late.
items.explanation: Ich komme zehn Minuten später: literally, I come ten minutes later.
